Aryani2020_word_arousal: People who rated kiki-like words rated them as more arousing than they rated bouba-like words.
Asch1946_warm_cold: People described with a "warm" personality trait were rated as more generous than people described with a "cold" personality trait.
Bauer2012_consumer_cues: People primed with a consumer identity rated other people as less partner-like (more instrumental, less relational) than people primed with an individual identity did.
BlackBarnes2015_transportation: People who read fiction reported greater narrative transportation than people who read nonfiction.
Cao2018_bayesian_pilot: People who read a description of a pilot were more likely to judge the pilot as a man than as a woman.
Chao2017_thankyou_gift: People who received a salient thank-you gift for an initial donation were less likely to make a subsequent donation than people who received no thank-you gift at all.
Cooney2016_fairness: People who anticipate a fair procedure predict they will feel happier than people who anticipate an unfair procedure.
Correll2007_motherhood_penalty: People who are portrayed as mothers are rated as less competent than people who are portrayed as non-mothers.
DeNeve1998_swb_neuroticism: People with higher subjective well-being report experiencing negative emotions less frequently than people with lower subjective well-being.
DogerliogluDemir2014_incidental_anchor: People exposed to a high anchor value stated a higher willingness to pay than people exposed to a low anchor value.
Eyal2008_moral_distance: People who judged moral transgressions framed as occurring in the distant future rated them as more wrong than people who judged the same transgressions framed as occurring in the near future.
FathKay2018_hierarchy_corruption: People in hierarchical organizations were expected to engage in corruption more than people in flat organizations.
Fetherstonhaugh1997_psychophysical_numbi: People in the small-camp condition rated their preference for Programme R more highly than people in the large-camp condition.
Finucane2000_affect_heuristic: People who perceive an activity or technology as having greater benefit judge its risk to be lower than people who perceive it as having less benefit.
Genschow2017_free_will_attribution: People induced to disbelieve in free will showed less correspondence bias (less tendency to attribute others' behavior to disposition over situation) than people in the control condition.
Glikson2017_smiley_competence: Senders of a work message that contains a smiley are rated as less competent than senders of the same message without a smiley.
Hoorens2015_more_less_asymmetry: People agree more with a "more than" comparative framing than with a "less than" framing when rating the same relationship or quantity.
Huang2019_anthropomorphism_holistic: People who were exposed to an anthropomorphized (vs. nonanthropomorphized) product chose the holistic-favored option A more often than those in the nonanthropomorphized condition.
Husnu2010_imagined_contact: People who imagined intergroup contact reported greater intentions to engage in future contact than people in the control condition.
John2016_hiding_information: People who revealed unsavory information about themselves were judged more favorably than those who hid it.
KimMarkus1999_uniqueness_preference: People who were told a figure belonged to a two-person minority subgroup rated that figure as more likeable than people who were told the figure belonged to the majority subgroup.
Klink2000_soundsymbolism: People who heard back-vowel-sounding names rated them as "richer" more than they rated front-vowel-sounding names as "richer."
Knobe2003_side_effect: People who learn about a side effect that harmed someone judged that side effect as caused intentionally more than people who learn about a side effect that helped someone.
McCullough2002_gratitude_agreeableness: People who scored higher in gratitude tended to score higher in agreeableness than those who scored lower in gratitude.
Mellers2001_conjunction_frequency: People judge that a conjunction of events (e.g., an unlikely event described together with a likely one, such as "and are") is more probable than the unlikely constituent event alone (such as "who are"), violating the conjunction rule.
Miyamoto2002_correspondence_bias: People who read or wrote an essay assigned to argue for a position were judged to hold attitudes more in line with that position than were people whose assigned essay argued against it.
Oppenheimer2009_retrospective_gambler: People who observe a rare three-sixes outcome infer a longer prior sequence of rolls than people who observe the more common two-dice two-sixes outcome.
Park2019_scarcity_price_quality: People who experienced scarcity relied on price to judge quality less than people in the control condition.
Paunonen2003_attractiveness_extraversion: People who are more physically attractive tend to be rated as more extraverted than people who are less physically attractive.
Peters2006_numeracy_framing: People who are less numerate showed a larger difference between gain-framed and loss-framed ratings than people who are more numerate.
Reinhard2013_unconscious_lie_detection: People engaged in unconscious thought before judging a lie detection task detected lies more accurately than people who engaged in conscious thought.
Rottenstreich2001_affective_lottery: People choosing between prizes framed with low-probability outcomes selected the affect-rich prize more often than people choosing between the same prizes framed as certain outcomes.
Stevenson2000_web_brand_attitude: People who had a more positive attitude toward the website rated the brand more positively than people who had a less positive attitude toward the website.
Tamir2012_selfdisclosure: People self-disclosing are willing to forgo more money to talk about themselves than people not self-disclosing.
Thoresen2003_commitment_negative_affect: People who reported higher occupational commitment tended to have lower negative emotionality than those with lower occupational commitment.
Tversky1973_availability_letters: People judge that words beginning with a given letter are more numerous than words having that same letter in the third position, even when the latter are actually more frequent.
Valdesolo2007_hypocrisy: People who judged their own or an ingroup member's transgression as more morally acceptable than the same transgression committed by another person or an outgroup member rated it as fairer than they rated others' identical transgressions.
Weinstein1984_comparative_optimism: People rate their own likelihood of experiencing negative future life events as lower than the likelihood they assign to their average peer experiencing those same events.
